Wider Sports News.body:
The 2026/2027 HSBC SVNS World Series will once again visit Dubai, Cape Town, Singapore, Perth, Vancouver and New York before culminating in the HSBC SVNS World Championship, which will be held across Hong Kong, Valladolid and Bordeaux.

The Dubai 7s will kick off the series on the 28th and 29th of November this year, followed by the Cape Town 7s on the 5th and 6th of December. The Singapore 7s will be played on the 30th and 31st of January 2027, followed by the Perth 7s on the 6th and 7th of February, the Vancouver 7s on the 6th and 7th of March, and the New York 7s on the 13th and 14th of March.

Wider Sports News.title: Beyond the purse: Inside Golf Saudi’s US$15m strategy to reshape women’s golf
Wider Sports News.summary: As PIF London Championship nears, Golf Saudi's US$15m Global Series is redrawing the commercial blueprint for women's professional golf. The post Beyond the purse: Inside Golf Saudi’s US$15m strategy to reshape women’s golf appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The global sports economy is changing, and women’s professional golf is leading the way. When the Ladies European Tour (LET) starts the PIF London Championship at Centurion Club in Hertfordshire from 6th to 9th August 6 2026, it will mark the sixth consecutive year of this event. This championship is more than just a top tournament; it represents a long-term strategy by Golf Saudi and the Public Investment Fund (PIF) aimed at transforming professional golf, creating inclusive communities, and making Saudi Arabia a centre for sports tourism.

For years, women’s professional sports faced challenges like limited funding, a lack of broadcast exposure, and fragmented sponsorship opportunities. Launched in 2021 as the Aramco Team Series, this initiative changed the situation by adding institutional support. Now part of the PIF Global Series, the LET’s financial foundation has been strengthened. For the 2026 season, the series will provide an unprecedented US$15 million in total prize money across five international events, providing the tour with economic stability.

Wider Sports News.title: Punjab Kings’ App engagement surges 9x year on year as franchise builds fan intelligence with SI
Wider Sports News.summary: As IPL franchises look beyond just media rights and sponsorship cycles, Punjab Kings used IPL 2026 to convert social reach into owned relationships, establish a fan intelligence capability and lay the foundation for fan-driven revenue streams. The post Punjab Kings’ App engagement surges 9x year on year as franchise builds fan intelligence with SI appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
For IPL franchises, the season represents the most valuable window in the sporting calendar, a concentrated period of unmatched fan attention, intent and engagement. Yet, as the league evolves commercially, the next phase of growth will increasingly be defined not by the scale of social reach alone, but by a franchise’s ability to convert moments of attention into lasting fan relationships and sustainable revenue opportunities.

This shift from borrowed audiences to owned ecosystems has become a strategic imperative for rights holders globally. Social platforms remain indispensable for discovery and distribution, but long-term enterprise value is created when fans transition into environments where franchises can engage them directly, understand their preferences, personalise experiences and unlock new avenues of monetisation.

Wider Sports News.title: Allianz to take over HSBC Life Singapore in deal including bancassurance partnership
Wider Sports News.summary: Allianz to take over HSBC Life Singapore in deal including bancassurance partnership Asia Insurance Review
Wider Sports News.body:
Allianz Group (Allianz) and HSBC Holdings (HSBC Group) today announced that Allianz, through its wholly owned subsidiary Allianz Asia Holding, has agreed to acquire HSBC Life Singapore, subject to regulatory approval.

HSBC Life Singapore is a Singapore-incorporated and licensed composite insurer with a strong presence in Singapore’s life and health insurance market. In addition, Allianz and HSBC Bank (Singapore) (HSBC Singapore) have agreed on a 15-year exclusive distribution partnership under which Allianz will provide protection, health, retirement and wealth solutions to HSBC’s customers in Singapore. The partnership builds on a well-established distribution relationship between Allianz and HSBC Group across Asia, and is expected to commence upon completion of the transaction.

Wider Sports News.title: TNT Sports adapts Olympic broadcast playbook to transform Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games
Wider Sports News.summary: TNT Sports has ended the BBC's stranglehold on the Commonwealth Games. WBD Sports Europe EVP Scott Young tells SportsPro about how it will use its Olympic creative and technical experience to make the Commonwealth Games a major streaming event. The post TNT Sports adapts Olympic broadcast playbook to transform Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
TNT Sports’ acquisition of the exclusive UK broadcast rights to the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games caught many by surprise when it was announced last December. The BBC had aired the quadrennial multi-sport event since television coverage began in 1954, an unbroken streak of 72 years, and blanket free-to-air (FTA) coverage has allowed previous UK-based Games in Manchester (2002), Glasgow (2014) and Birmingham (2022) to become significant cultural events.

The BBC’s inability or unwillingness to beat TNT Sports’ bid was viewed either as evidence of financial pressures facing the public service broadcaster (PSB) or the reduced appeal of a scaled back Commonwealth Games when compared to previous years, necessitated by the withdrawal of original host Victoria three years ago.

Rugby.title: WRU officially confirm they will axe either Ospreys or Scarlets
Rugby.summary: The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has officially confirmed that Welsh rugby will move to a three-team professional model from the start of the 2028/29 season...
Rugby.body:
The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has officially confirmed that Welsh rugby will move to a three-team professional model from the start of the 2028/29 season, with either the Ospreys or Scarlets set to effectively be axed.

The WRU announced its future operating model on Wednesday, outlining plans for one professional team in the capital, one in east Wales and one in west Wales. The governing body has already indicated that Cardiff Rugby and Dragons RFC are in line for two of those licences, leaving the Ospreys and Scarlets effectively competing for a single place in west Wales.

Rugby.body:
Two-cap England Red Roses wing Bo Westcombe Evans has joined Trailfinders Women ahead of the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby campaign. To date the 24-year-old has spent the entirety of her senior career in the East Midlands with Loughborough Lightning. Last season Westcombe Evans was PWR’s joint-top try-scorer, having crossed the whitewash 12 times in 16 league appearances.

It was Westcombe Evans’ first season back after a year out of rugby with an ACL injury sustained in 2024. The injury occurred just weeks after the wing made her Red Roses debut at the 2024 edition of WXV1 and scored her maiden Test rugby try against the USA Women’s Eagles.

Rugby.title: Six England players who could theoretically jump ship to different Test nations
Rugby.summary: World Rugby’s three-year stand-down rule has reshaped international rugby.
Rugby.body:
World Rugby’s three-year stand-down rule has reshaped international rugby. The regulation allows captured players to switch allegiance after 36 months in the Test wilderness, provided they hold the necessary birthright or residency qualifications.

For a handful of former England stars, that window is either wide open or rapidly approaching. The most high-profile name in the rumour mill had been Owen Farrell. The 34-year-old, who won the last of his 112 England caps in the 2023 Rugby World Cup third-place play-off, completes his three-year stand-down this October. But despite his father Andy coaching Ireland, a switch to green is not happening. Farrell does not meet World Rugby’s birthright criteria as his Irish heritage traces back to a great-grandparent, not a parent or grandparent.

Rugby.title: Deep parallels to 2010 for the All Blacks ahead of South Africa
Rugby.summary: It was crisis mode for the All Blacks that triggered an introspective look at the team's tactics, selections and operations. From a kick-heavy game in 2009, they adopted a more expansive, high-risk game.
Rugby.body:
2009 was a great year for South African rugby. It was the year they conquered everyone, from a 2-1 series win in the famous British & Irish Lions tour, to a 3-0 ‘black-wash’ over the All Blacks on the way to a Tri Nations title. After winning the Rugby World Cup in 2007, by 2009 the Boks were sailing high.

The first two Tests at home against New Zealand the boot of Morne Steyn fuelled points while an uncompromising defence and kick pressure choked the All Blacks out of the games.

Rugby.title: Asian Games sevens fixtures confirmed ahead of critical step to Olympics
Rugby.summary: The 2026 Asian Games - the 20th iteration of the sporting event - is set to kick off in Japan in October.
Rugby.body:
The 2026 Asian Games – the 20th iteration of the sporting event – is set to kick off in Japan in October, marking a critical juncture for sevens sides in the region. With the final confirmed list of teams and pools drawn late last week, the Asian Games marks a critical fixture for unions in the region, the event marking a major stop on the way to the Olympics, both for on-field performances and being linked to funding from respective Olympic committees off the field.

The event will form part of a busy two months of sevens action in the region, falling in between two legs of the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series taking place in the Chinese city of Suzhou (29th-30th August) and Sri Lanka’s largest city, Colombo (17th-18th October).

Rugby.title: Rugby World Cups get $90m boost from Australian government, Pacific to benefit
Rugby.summary: Part of Rugby Australia's $90 million World Cup government injection will be spent in the Pacific, breathing life into the code after Moana's controversial Super Rugby exit.
Rugby.body:
Part of Rugby Australia’s $90 million World Cup government injection will be spent in the Pacific, breathing life into the code after Moana’s controversial Super Rugby exit. The package will support the delivery of both next year’s home men’s World Cup and the 2029 women’s showpiece but will also help fund legacy projects focused on the women’s game in Australia and competition in the Pacific.

It follows the Australian government’s $600m investment in the NRL’s Papua New Guinea franchise, set to launch in 2028. Rugby Australia boss Phil Waugh was in Brisbane on Wednesday to spruik the federal government injection ahead of both events.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga named on Canterbury bench for NPC return
Rugby.summary: Returning All Blacks star Richie Mo'unga will be eased back into NPC rugby off the bench as the headliner of the first team namings of the new provincial season.
Rugby.body:
Returning All Blacks star Richie Mo’unga will be eased back into NPC rugby off the bench as the headliner of the first team namings of the new provincial season. Mo’unga’s Canterbury side features All Blacks Sevens flyer-turned-Highlanders playmaker Andrew Knewstubb at No.10, with Chay Fihaki at fullback. Newly capped All Black Jamie Hannah will run out as a starting lock, with breakthrough Blues rookie Torian Barnes named at No.8, and new Canterbury captain Brodie McAlister at hooker. Mo’unga will wear the No.22 jersey in what will be his first game at Christchurch’s new One New Zealand Stadium.

Canterbury will square off with an Auckland team that features Stephen Perofeta as the starting No.10, with capped All Black Angus Ta’avao-Matau also in the run-on side. Ofa Tu’ungafasi is on the bench alongside newly capped Maori All Black Payton Spencer and ex-Wallaby Issak Fines-Leleiwasa.

Rugby.title: Five All Blacks talking points from the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry squad
Rugby.summary: Dave Rennie's 44-man All Blacks squad was unveiled on Monday, and while it featured just three new faces, it inevitably raised plenty more eyebrows.
Rugby.body:

Rugby.summary: Sam Cane says he is "stoked" to see ex-teammate Luke Jacobson performing in the black jersey he once wore, sharing high praise for the Chiefs captain as a man who lives up to his 'Concrete Shoulders' nickname.
Rugby.body:
Sam Cane says he is “stoked” to see ex-teammate Luke Jacobson performing in the black jersey he once wore, sharing high praise for the Chiefs captain as a man who lives up to his ‘Concrete Shoulders’ nickname.

Jacobson’s journey to the All Blacks‘ No.7 jersey has been long, hard-fought, and plagued by injuries. Yet, seven years on from his debut and with just 26 Tests in that span, he has now been rewarded for his patience with three consecutive starts in one of rugby’s most famed shirts.

Rugby.body:
Wallaroos winger Desiree Miller has been ruled out of the NSW Waratahs’ Super Rugby Champions Final against the Blues, seeing Amelia Whitaker brought in to the run-on side for the clash with the Super Rugby Aupiki winners in Sydney.

Miller will not play in the Champions Final on Saturday evening, having picked up a calf injury in the Super Rugby Women’s Grand Final triumph over the Fijian Drua in Ba. That result secured another three-peat for the Tahs, and their seventh title in less than 10 years.

Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach has revealed the plan for first five Beauden Barrett with the veteran set to play the first game of the tour. Barrett was the first choice starter under Robertson last year but the 144-Test veteran did not feature across the July Nations Championships fixtures with the All Blacks preferring Ruben Love to start and using Damian McKenzie as cover from fullback.

Rennie said it was “tough for him” to sit out the July fixtures but he proved to be the ultimate professional guiding the others in preparation. “Well, Beauden will start against the Stormers. There you go. There’s a little leg up,” Rennie confirmed to media at this week’s squad announcement.

Rugby.summary: Former Exeter Chiefs inside centre Tamati Tua has secured a move to Japan Rugby League One Division One outfit Ricoh Black Rams Tokyo for next season.
Rugby.body:
Former Exeter Chiefs inside centre Tamati Tua has secured a move to Japan Rugby League One Division One outfit Ricoh Black Rams Tokyo for next season after being released by Rob Baxter when his contract ran out at the end of June.

Tua, 28, who can also play outside centre and left wing, was a target for Toulon and Perpignan before missing the whole of last season after an operation on an Achilles tendon he ruptured in training in August.

Rugby.title: Report: Joe Schmidt set for temporary return to Irish rugby
Rugby.summary: Schmidt's reputation as one of the finest minds in the game has remained largely intact, despite winning just 12 of his 30 Tests in charge of Australia.
Rugby.body:
Now that Joe Schmidt’s tenure as Wallabies head coach has ended, speculation about his next move has never been far away. And, according to The Australian, the 60-year-old Kiwi will soon be heading back to Ireland, where he enjoyed a trophy-laden spell with the national team and Leinster, as a consultant to Ulster.

In six years under him, Ireland won three Six Nations, including a Grand Slam in 2018. Ireland were ranked No.1 in the World Rugby Rankings for the first time in their history in 2019, and recorded their first-ever wins over New Zealand. With Leinster, he won four titles in three seasons, including back-to-back European Cups.

Rugby.summary: The former Harlequins and Leicester Tigers boss joined Stade from Benetton in June 2022 as defence coach, a role he had previously held with Saracens and England.
Rugby.body:
Stade Français have opened talks with head coach Paul Gustard about extending his stay in the French capital after overseeing a remarkable transformation in the club’s fortunes.

The former Harlequins and Leicester Tigers boss joined Stade from Benetton in June 2022 as defence coach, a role he had previously held with Saracens and England. In October 2024, he was promoted to head coach following Karim Ghezal’s departure and guided them to safety, finishing 12th, one point clear of Perpignan and the relegation play-off.

Rugby.summary: They did, however, benefit from the decision, clinching their third straight Super Rugby Aupiki title at the new One New Zealand Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Blues assistant coach Carlos Spencer has revealed his emotions during Tara Turner’s decision to take a quick tap in the 82nd minute of the Super Rugby Aupiki final against Matatu.

They did, however, benefit from the decision, clinching their third straight Super Rugby Aupiki title at the new One New Zealand Stadium. Their triumph, a nail-biting 28-21 victory over the Christchurch-based side, came after the Blues earned a penalty deep inside Matatu’s 22-metre line, a minute after the final hooter, with the scores equal at 21 apiece.

Rugby.body:
Aseza Hele is back in Swys de Bruin’s Springbok Women squad for the first time since Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025. Last time the back-row played Test rugby was when South Africa exited the Women’s Rugby World Cup with a quarter-final loss to the Black Ferns.

Rugby.body:
In September a new era for women’s rugby will begin when the WXV Global Series sets sail for the very first time. The top 18 ranked teams in the world will face-off across an eight-week global window between 12 September to 31 October. The 12 top-ranked sides in the world – Australia, Canada, England, France, Italy, Ireland, Japan, New Zealand, Scotland, South Africa, USA, and Wales – will take part in the home-and-away cross-regional touring WXV Global Series.

It has also been confirmed that Mitsubishi Electric is the presenting partner of the WXV Global Series and WXV Global Series Challenger. Over 100 women’s Test matches will be played ahead of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2029 in Australia – 36 Test matches will be played across September and October this year.

Rugby.title: Champions Saints host Newcastle on opening weekend
Rugby.summary: Prem champions Northampton host Newcastle on the opening weekend of the 2026-27 season, with Exeter at home to Gloucester.
Rugby.body:
Champions Northampton will host Newcastle Red Bulls on the opening day of the 2026-27 Prem rugby season. Saints beat Exeter to lift the trophy for the second time in three seasons in June and start the new campaign at home on Friday, 25 September.

The Chiefs are also at home for their first game, with Gloucester set to visit Sandy Park on the Saturday. Elsewhere across the opening weekend, Harlequins are at home to Bath on Friday, Sale host Bristol on Saturday evening and Leicester play Saracens in the only match on Sunday.

Rugby.title: PREM fixtures: Northampton start title defence at home; Monday rugby returns
Rugby.summary: The new season will start on Friday, 25 September and finish with the final at Allianz Stadium, on Saturday, 19 June.
Rugby.body:
The 2026/27 PREM season, the ninth with Gallagher as the title sponsor, will kick off with a clash between last season’s top and bottom club, as reigning champions Northampton take on the re-energised Newcastle Red Bulls at Franklin’s Gardens, on Friday, 25 September.

New Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland couldn’t have asked for a more difficult start to his reign in charge, with the ex-Ulster man’s first-ever PREM game as a head coach pitting him against English rugby’s most dominant force in recent times.

Rugby.title: Argentina select 10 Test rookies in squad for Boks and Wallabies clashes
Rugby.summary: Ten uncapped players are included in Felipe Contepomi's 36-strong Pumas squad for the one-off Test against South Africa and the two-Test series against Australia.
Rugby.body:
Having failed to play any of the five uncapped members of his Nations Championship squad during July, Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi looks certain to blood some new talent in the upcoming Test against South Africa and the two-match series against Australia. These matches fill the gap left in the calendar by The Rugby Championship not being played in 2026.

The Pumas take on world champions South Africa at the José Amalfitani Stadium in Buenos Aires on 8 August, before hosting the Wallabies in Jujuy, on 29 August, and Mendoza, on 5 September.

Rugby.title: The area of Tupou’s game that has ‘definitely added value’ to Wallabies
Rugby.summary: 91-Test Wallabies prop Allan Alaalatoa believes Taniela Tupou had already added value at the set-piece this international season.
Rugby.body:
91-Test Wallabies prop Allan Alaalatoa believes Taniela Tupou had already added value at the set-piece this international season, citing that as an area of his teammate’s game that has benefited from a stint abroad in France.

Tupou is back Down Under after making a dozen appearances for Top 14 side Racing 92, having signed a deal through to 2028 with the Parisian club. The front-rower last donned the sky blue and white hoops in a heavy semi-final loss to eventual champions Toulouse last month.

Rugby.title: Former England Lock George Kruis Helps Set 28-Hour Rugby Sevens World Record
Rugby.summary: Former England Lock George Kruis Helps Set 28-Hour Rugby Sevens World Record Read Rugby Union
Rugby.body:
Former England lock George Kruis has demonstrated the ultimate endurance by helping break a provisional Guinness World Record in a grueling 28-hour rugby sevens match for charity.

The extraordinary charity match took place at Sandbach RUFC, where players pushed their bodies to the absolute limit. According to The Rugby Paper, the event aimed to raise crucial funds for mental health and community causes, drawing massive local support throughout the day and night.

Rugby.title: Cohen Norrie: 'I’ve always dreamed of playing for Auckland'
Rugby.summary: “Personally, I’ve always dreamed of playing for Auckland. Having the opportunity to become a fulltime rugby player was a huge lesson and privilege.
Rugby.body:
He made seven appearances in his debut season for Auckland last year, starting three of the last four games. The first was a 52-29 win against Manawata, where he scored a try and earned man-of-the-match despite being notified only 10 minutes before kickoff that he was playing.

Norrie won the Auckland Emerging Player of the Year and was identified as one of the Most Promising Players of the Year in the New Zealand Rugby Almanack. Yet Auckland were awful, winning only two of ten matches, the worst season the 17-time champions have endured in 50 years of the NPC.

Rugby.title: USA Men's Eagles report card: All 29 Nations Cup players rated
Rugby.summary: The USA Men’s Eagles have flown through the first block of World Rugby Nations Cup Tests with an unbeaten 3-0 record.
Rugby.body:
The USA Men’s Eagles have flown through the first block of World Rugby Nations Cup Tests with an unbeaten 3-0 record, overcoming a series of opponents all bound for Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 in Australia.

Chris Hilsenbeck was the hero for the USA in a 30-29 thriller against Portugal to open the team’s campaign in the all-new competition, with the fly-half slotting a long-range penalty at the death to all but secure the win.

Rugby.title: Indian Rugby Teams Set for Asia Rugby Sevens Trophy in Nepal, Led by Captains Shikha Yadav and Mohit Khatri
Rugby.summary: Indian Rugby Teams Set for Asia Rugby Sevens Trophy in Nepal, Led by Captains Shikha Yadav and Mohit Khatri News On AIR
Rugby.body:
The Indian Rugby men’s and women’s teams will be competing at the Asia Rugby Sevens Trophy in Nepal beginning tomorrow. Shikha Yadav and Mohit Khatri having been named captains for their respective teams.

The Indian men’s team is scheduled to start their campaign against Bangladesh, while the women will lock horns with Sri Lanka to begin a promising campaign tomorrow.The Indian women’s team is looking to convert their streak of silver medals from the last three years into gold. On the other hand, the men’s team which finished fifth last year are looking to better their performance.

Rugby.title: The All Blacks captain shouldn't need a rest after a sabbatical
Rugby.summary: If Ardie Savea has a personal or family issue to attend to, fine. The birth of a child, good as gold. But if the All Blacks captain is really missing the start of the team's tour to South Africa so he can freshen up, then I'm unimpressed.
Rugby.body:
If Ardie Savea has a personal or family issue to attend to, fine. The birth of a child, good as gold. But if the All Blacks captain is really missing the start of the team’s tour to South Africa so he can freshen up, then I’m unimpressed.

Savea, as we all know, is an incredibly hard-working player. Not especially big or quick, the loose forward has willed himself into being world-class. By dint of also being among the top handful of New Zealand’s players, he’s going to be picked for all the games that matter.

Rugby.title: Fabian Holland: 'I'm excited to rip in, body feels mint'
Rugby.summary: Holland said it's been a tough road back from injury, and that he had to adjust his mindset throughout the journey.
Rugby.body:
23-year-old Highlanders lock Fabian Holland is back in the All Blacks mix after missing the whole of the Super Rugby Pacific season through a shoulder injury. The reigning World Rugby Men’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year was named in Dave Rennie’s All Blacks squad for the Greatest Rivalry Tour, as one of the ten additional players.

Rennie added ten players to his original 34-man Nations Championship squad for the upcoming tour of South Africa, which included Holland, after his 40-minute hit-out for Otago on Friday against Mid Canterbury.

Rugby.title: Ex-NRL flyer returns to Australia Sevens with LA Olympics in sight
Rugby.summary: Two-time Olympian Nathan Lawson will be back with the Australia Men’s Sevens program after a stint with NRL outfit the St George Illawarra Dragons.
Rugby.body:
Two-time Olympian Nathan Lawson will soon be back with the Australia Men’s Sevens program after a stint with NRL outfit the St George Illawarra Dragons, committing to Rugby Australia ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Rugby Australia announced this week that Lawson has penned a deal with the national sevens program, but the dual-code athlete will first return to the sport via the all-new Ultimate Sevens in Europe later this year.

Rugby.title: Ex-All Black: Don't mistake Semisi Tupou Ta'eiloa for a one-trick pony
Rugby.summary: Semisi Tupou Ta'eiloa was one of three new faces unveiled in the All Blacks' 44-man squad for the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Tour, and ex-All Black James Parsons believes it's a selection that ticks some big boxes in Dave Rennie's system.
Rugby.body:
Semisi Tupou Ta’eiloa was one of three new faces unveiled in the All Blacks‘ 44-man squad for the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour, and ex-All Black James Parsons believes it’s a selection that ticks some big boxes in Dave Rennie’s system.

The 22-year-old enjoyed a breakthrough Super Rugby Pacific campaign in just his first season in the competition last year, winning the starting No.8 jersey and pushing Ardie Savea to the openside flank after just one game. From there, the Southland star was the most highly employed ball-carrier in the competition by a comfortable margin, taking the ball into contact 205 times in 13 games, and scoring seven tries.

Rugby.title: Rugby players finish 28-hour world record attempt in Sandbach
Rugby.summary: Rugby players finish 28-hour world record attempt in Sandbach BBC
Rugby.body:
Provisional world records have been set simultaneously for the longest ever men and women's rugby sevens matches. The two games were played at Sandbach Rugby Club in Cheshire over Friday and Saturday, with both contests lasting 28 hours.

For the men's match, the duration was longer than the current Guinness World Record of 24 hours and 30 minutes set in 2017, while there was not an existing record for a women's match.

Rugby.title: Seilala Mapusua secures new job after Moana Pasifika exit
Rugby.summary: Former Samoa centre and head coach Seilala Mapusua has joined Japan Rugby League One outfit, Kubota Spears, as an assistant coach.
Rugby.body:
Former Samoa centre and head coach Seilala Mapusua has joined Japan Rugby League One outfit, Kubota Spears, as an assistant coach. It marks a return to Kubota for Mapusua, who played there in the latter stages of his decorated career.

Mapusua had been on the lookout for a new job since Moana Pasifika folded at the end of the Super Rugby season and is now part of head coach Frans Ludeke’s coaching team. “I feel immense joy and excitement at this new challenge, returning to Kubota Spears Funabashi Tokyo-Bay as a coach, 15 years after joining as a player,” said Mapusua, who moved to Kubota from London Irish in 2011 in his playing days.

Rugby.title: Former Great Britain captain Fergusson lands Celtic Challenge coaching role
Rugby.summary: Former Great Britain Sevens captain Robbie Fergusson has been named Glasgow Warriors head coach ahead of the 2026/27 Celtic Challenge season.
Rugby.body:
Former Great Britain Sevens captain Robbie Fergusson has been named Glasgow Warriors head coach ahead of the 2026/27 Celtic Challenge season. The 32-year-old, who has most recently worked as an assistant with the Hong Kong China Sevens and has also worked as an assistant with Great Britain Women’s Sevens. He also spent two spells with Glasgow in his playing career.

Fergusson has also preciously been Director of Rugby of Ayr RFC and the Ayrshire Bulls. During his time with his hometown club he oversaw their senior and pathway programmes. He retired in 2024 to conclude his nine-year career. Fergusson made over 50 appearances on the HSBC SVNS Series, competed at the 2020 Olympic Games in Tokyo and at two Commonwealth Games for Scotland.

Rugby.summary: Zac Lomax has vowed that the PNG Chiefs will shock the NRL when they enter the competition in 2028 after penning a three-year contract, but it is not all good news for the expansion outfit.
Rugby.body:
Zac Lomax has vowed that the PNG Chiefs will shock the NRL when they enter the competition in 2028 after penning a three-year contract, but it is not all good news for the expansion outfit.

The Chiefs had made Queensland Reds rising star Treyvon Pritchard, who is tipped for superstardom, a target, but instead of switching codes, he has agreed a new deal with the Super Rugby outfit and Rugby Australia.

Rugby.title: 2026 Swyftx Super Rugby Women’s | RugbyPass' Team of the Season
Rugby.summary: The NSW Waratahs claimed a third Super Rugby Women's title in a row with an emphatic 34-17 win over the Fijian Drua in Ba.
Rugby.body:
The NSW Waratahs claimed a third Super Rugby Women’s title in a row with an emphatic 34-17 win over the Fijian Drua in Ba. A first-ever Final held on the islands the stage was set for Drua success as 4,097 supporters lined the stands. But when the final curtain fell, it was the Waratahs’ day as a third consecutive league title made its way back to Sydney.

Wallaroos stalwarts Maya Steward and Desiree Miller both made their way over the whitewash at Four R Stadium, teenage starlet Amelia Whitaker dotted down twice in the final 20 minutes and Rosie Ferguson scored one try.

Exeter Chiefs have confirmed that they have signed former Gloucester and England U20s loosehead Archie McArthur, who was released by the Kingsholm outfit when his contract ran out at the end of June.

Rugby.summary: Ex-England lock George Kruis helps set Rugby Sevens world record after 28-hour challenge The Rugby Paper
Rugby.body:
Former England lock George Kruis was among the players who helped set a provisional Guinness World Record for the longest men’s Rugby Sevens match after a marathon 28-hour challenge at Sandbach RUFC.

The 24/7s event in Cheshire saw men’s and women’s teams come together to raise awareness and funds for rugby mental health charity LooseHeadz, with more than £68,500 donated so far.

Rugby.title: Lowe signs for Suntory Sungoliath after Leinster exit
Rugby.summary: Tokyo Suntory Sungoliath confirm the signing of former Ireland and Leinster wing James Lowe on a two-year deal.
Rugby.body:
Tokyo Suntory Sungoliath have confirmed the signing of former Ireland and Leinster wing James Lowe on a two-year deal. Lowe departed Irish rugby at the end of the 2025-26 season after failing to agree a contract extension with Leinster, for whom he scored a record 71 tries.

The 34-year-old won two Six Nations titles with Ireland, including the Grand Slam, and played at the 2023 World Cup. The New Zealand-born back also won a Champions Cup and six United Rugby Championship titles with Leinster and played two Tests for the British and Irish Lions in last year's series win over the Wallabies in Australia.

Rugby.title: All Blacks reunite with former assistant ahead of South Africa tour
Rugby.summary: The Maori All Blacks head coach led his side to a 38-31 victory over the Japan XV at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya, Japan last month.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie and the All Blacks have called in former assistant and current Maori All Blacks head coach Tamati Ellison for the upcoming Greatest Rivalry Tour of South Africa. Ellison, who was announced as Jason Holland’s Blues assistant for the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season, will re-join the All Blacks camp ahead of the tour, the same environment he left in March 2026.

The 43-year-old former All Blacks assistant began as the skills coach during Scott Robertson’s two-year tenure, before becoming the team’s defence coach during the 2025 season.

Rugby.body:

Mchunu joins the team’s preparations for the one-off Test against Argentina and the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry (RGR) series against New Zealand as the Springboks leap back into Test match mode following a week off.

Rugby.summary: The Blues successfully defended their Super Rugby Aupiki title for a third consecutive year with a thrilling 28-21 win over Matatu in the final at Te Kaha/One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch.
Rugby.body:
The Blues successfully defended their Super Rugby Aupiki title for a third consecutive year with a thrilling 28-21 win over Matatu in the final at Te Kaha/One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch.

With 20 wins in 30 games, the Blues have the best record in the competition, but it took some late, daring rugby to prevail in 2026. While Matatu impressed by winning a club-record four consecutive matches to top the round-robin standings, the Hurricanes Poua were arguably the darlings of the competition, improving out of sight.

Rugby.title: ITV confirmed as 2027 Rugby World Cup broadcaster
Rugby.summary: ITV will show next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia, extending the broadcaster's coverage of the tournament to a 10th successive edition.
Rugby.body:
ITV will show next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia, extending the broadcaster's coverage of the tournament to a 10th successive edition. All 52 matches from the event, which features 24 teams and a last-16 knockout round, will be shown live.

"This is much more than a new agreement with a trusted partner, it is a statement of intent to ensure that everyone in the UK can experience and be inspired by one of the world's iconic sporting events, its action, drama and personalities," said World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin.

Rugby.summary: The France men’s and Poland women’s teams claimed the Rugby Europe 7s Championship Series 2026 titles, coming out on top after two highly competitive legs hosted by Hamburg and Split.
Rugby.body:
The France men’s and Poland women’s teams claimed the Rugby Europe 7s Championship Series 2026 titles, coming out on top after two highly competitive legs hosted by Hamburg and Split.

Rugby.title: Exeter sign prop McArthur from Gloucester
Rugby.summary: Gloucester's loosehead prop joins last season's Prem runner's up as cover for the departing Scott Sio.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs have signed loosehead prop Archie McArthur from Gloucester for the 2026-27 season. McArthur made 20 appearances for the Cherry and Whites during three campaigns while being dual-registered with Champ side Hartpury, who he also played 25 games for.

The 23-year-old began his career in Wasps' academy and has also represented England at under-20s level. "He's played against us a few times interestingly, so we watched those games in detail and saw him doing very well," Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter told the club website, external.

Rugby.title: ITV remains the home of the Men's Rugby World Cup in the UK
Rugby.summary: All 52 matches from Men's Rugby World Cup 2027 will be broadcast free-to-air in the UK.
Rugby.body:
All 52 matches from Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 will be broadcast live on free-to-air TV in the United Kingdom following a landmark agreement between World Rugby and ITV. ITV has been unveiled as the exclusive UK broadcast partner, continuing the station’s longstanding commitment to the third biggest sporting event in the world, which dates back to the second edition of the tournament in 1991.

The announcement comes soon after the southern hemisphere series of the Nations Championship, which was given blanket treatment by ITV. ITV Director of Sport, Niall Sloane said: “This is a monumental deal for audiences across the UK delivering coverage on ITV of the biggest rugby tournament. We’ve enjoyed a longstanding partnership with World Rugby and this will continue to thrive. This partnership further secures ITV as the home of rugby adding to our extensive portfolio and commitment of rugby coverage across ITV1, ITVX and ITV Sport YouTube.”

Rugby.title: Why Rieko Ioane needed Leinster stint after finding himself in a 'rut'
Rugby.summary: The 29-year-old last played for the All Blacks under former head coach Scott Robertson, during 2025's end-0f-year tour against Wales in Cardiff.
Rugby.body:
88-Test All Black veteran Rieko Ioane has revealed part of the reason why he jetted off to Ireland for a short-term sabbatical at Leinster. Ioane’s return to the All Blacks comes after a season-long move to Irish club Leinster, after spending most, if not all, of his career to date with the Blues and Auckland.

All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie included the versatile outside-back in his 44-man squad to take on South Africa in the upcoming Greatest Rivalry Tour, which starts next Friday against the Stormers in Cape Town.

Rugby.title: ‘We belong on this level’: The rise of the Denmark Sevens side
Rugby.summary: Riahi and Elmbak were both humbly confident about the realities of entering the top tier of the European Championships.
Rugby.body:
They may not be known as an international 7s powerhouse yet, but Denmark 7s announced themselves into the top flight of European 7s in the first leg of the 2026 Rugby Europe Championship competition, placing ninth from twelve on their debut tournament.

It’s an impressive start considering four years ago they were placing tenth in the second tier Trophy competition. Since then, the programme has risen quietly through the Rugby Europe ranks, from tenth to eighth in the 2023 Trophy, to joint second in the 2024 Trophy before securing the highest ever finish at international level for Danish rugby in 2025, placing second in the Trophy and securing promotion behind Türkiye.

Rugby.title: Why the All Blacks were forced into 'obvious' call to leave Ardie Savea home
Rugby.summary: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea will miss the early stages of the tour to South Africa with Rennie and his coaching team making a strategic decision to leave him home.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks captain Ardie Savea will miss the early stages of the tour to South Africa with Rennie and his coaching team making a strategic decision to leave him home. Dave Rennie explained that the cumulation of his playing time since last year his meant a 19-month continous season for Savea, starting with his campaign with Moana Pasifika in 2025.

Off the back of the international season with the All Blacks last year, Savea rolled straight into his commitments with Kobe Steelers in Japan as part of his sabbatical. “Ardie’s been training and playing since January 2025,” Rennie explained.

Rugby.title: 'Dupes is a good player': Why Ethan Blackadder was recalled to All Blacks and Kirifi missed out again
Rugby.summary: The announcement of the 44-man touring squad to South Africa featured a number of surprises in the loose forwards including Crusaders hard man Ethan Blackadder.
Rugby.body:
The announcement of the 44-man touring squad to South Africa featured a number of surprises in the loose forwards including Crusaders hard man Ethan Blackadder who found his way back into the squad.

Blackadder won his place over the likes of Hurricanes openside Du’Plessis Kirifi who went on to lead the Hurricanes to the Super Rugby title this year. The last of Blackadder’s 14 Tests was in fact in South Africa in 2024, the 31-27 loss to the Springboks at Ellis Park under former coach Scott Robertson.

Rugby.title: 'Couldn't stop shaking': Why Dave Rennie called up Semisi Tupou Ta'ieloa
Rugby.summary: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has detailed the shock that newly selected All Black squad member Semisi Tupou Ta'ieloa had when he received a call on Sunday afternoon.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has detailed the shock that newly selected All Black squad member Semisi Tupou Ta’ieloa had when he received a call on Sunday afternoon. The Moana Pasifika No.8 was one of three new names in the 44-man touring squad for South Africa, with the surprise selection a true bolter earning a spot over other capped loose forwards like Du’Plessis Kirifi.

Tupou Ta’ieloa was a standout for a struggling Moana Pasifika outfit, with his ball carrying and power proving very hard for opposition teams to stop. Rennie believed that they would get something different out of the 22-year-old Southland product.

Rugby.title: Rugby Australia ward off NRL offers to secure generational teenage talent long-term
Rugby.summary: The Queensland Reds back, still just 19 and off contract after next Super Rugby Pacific season, had been courted heavily by the NRL's Sydney Roosters and newcomers PNG.
Rugby.body:
Treyvon Pritchard will remain in rugby after the “generational talent” knocked back huge NRL interest to instead pursue his Wallabies dreams. The Queensland Reds back, still just 19 and off contract after next Super Rugby Pacific season, had been courted heavily by the NRL’s Sydney Roosters and newcomers PNG.

But, while the Chiefs were trumpeting the signing of code-hopper Zac Lomax over the weekend, it’s understood Pritchard was knocking back NRL offers and agreeing to a long-term deal with Rugby Australia.

Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie, selector Sir Graham Henry, and senior assistant Neil Barnes have opted for three debutants among their additional ten players to take on South Africa in the Greatest Rivalry Tour.

Rugby.title: Fijian Drua snap up Crusaders and former All Black assistant Brad Mooar
Rugby.summary: "I've loved being part of this club and working alongside such great people. Thank you to everyone who has supported me during my time here," Mooar said in a Crusaders media release.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks and Crusaders assistant Brad Mooar has put pen to paper with the Fijian Drua, becoming their head coach for the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season. The Crusaders assistant has signed a two-year deal with the Fijian Super Rugby Pacific franchise, leaving his role with the Canterbury-based franchise after six seasons as part of the coaching staff.

Mooar has played a part in four Super Rugby titles during his coaching stint, after two years with the All Blacks under Ian Foster in the 2020-2022 period. “I’ve loved being part of this club and working alongside such great people. Thank you to everyone who has supported me during my time here,” Mooar said in a Crusaders media release.

Rugby.title: Report: Moana Pasifika's Semisi Tupou Ta'eiloa tipped to make All Blacks squad
Rugby.summary: Uncapped Moana Pasifika forward Semisi Tupou Ta'eiloa has been tipped to make the All Blacks squad according to a report.
Rugby.body:
Uncapped Moana Pasifika forward Semisi Tupou Ta’eiloa has been tipped to make the All Blacks squad according to a report. The 23-year-old blockbusting No.8 is likely to be picked according to New Zealand news outlet The Post, with a report suggesting that he will make the 44-man group after signing with NZR.

Ta’eiloa was one of the most destructive ball carriers in Super Rugby Pacific this season, finishing in the top 10 for most carries and top 10 for defenders beaten. His new deal until the end of 2028 with NZR makes him eligible for selection with his physical ball carrying adding another dimension to the loose forward crops.

Rugby.title: 'Can only live off reputation for so long': Ex-Bok coach questions Eben Etzebeth's place in side
Rugby.summary: Springboks lock Eben Etzebeth is under pressure to retain his place in the top Springbok side after a long stint of the sidelines.
Rugby.body:
Springboks lock Eben Etzebeth is under pressure to retain his place in the top Springbok side after a long stint of the sidelines according to former Springbok coach Nick Mallett.

The 34-year-old hasn’t played a Test since November after being suspended for 12 weeks following a melee against Wales. The lock was named to play against England but was a late withdrawal before missing all three Tests, while he missed significant time with the Sharks during the URC season.

Rugby.title: All Black great Ma'a Nonu leaves Toulon for new role at South African club
Rugby.summary: All Black great Ma'a Nonu will join South African club Hollywood Bet Sharks after finishing his second stint with Top 14 club Toulon.
Rugby.body:
All Black great Ma’a Nonu will join South African club Hollywood Bet Sharks after finishing his second stint with Top 14 club Toulon. South African media have floated the idea of Nonu taking the field should Springbok midfielder Andre Esterhuizen be called up by the Boks.

“Ma’a Nonu will spend the next few months in Durban as part of a high-performance mentorship programme designed to accelerate the development of the club’s next generation of players by exposing them to one of the most successful leaders in world rugby,” the Sharks said.

Rugby.title: Channel Islands score six tries to beat Poland
Rugby.summary: The Channel Islands rugby union team beat Poland 38-27 in their second annual "international" match.
Rugby.body:
The Channel Islands rugby union team beat Poland 38-27 in their second annual "international" match. Jack McFarlane crossed in the left corner to give the hosts a ninth-minute lead, but two Dan Tomanek penalties saw Poland go 6-5 up after 16 minutes.

Anthony Armstrong went over on the right wing to put the islands 10-6 up midway through the first half. Charlie Wilkinson was mauled over shortly before half-time after Polish prop Peet Vorster had been sent to the sin-bin.

Rugby.title: Fissler Confidential: James O'Connor deal close; French points-machine in big demand
Rugby.summary: James O’Connor is understood to be set to return to Western Force to finish his career where it began, when he became the youngest-ever Super Rugby debutant at 17 in 2008.
Rugby.body:
James O’Connor is understood to be set to return to Western Force to finish his career where it began, when he became the youngest-ever Super Rugby debutant at 17 in 2008. The veteran Wallaby, who spent last season with Leicester Tigers, had been linked with one of his former club’s Queensland Reds, the NSW Waratahs and United Rugby Championship outfit the Sharks, since it was announced that he was leaving Welford Road.

He picked up the Western Force ‘Rookie of the Year’ award in 2009, winning the first of his Wallabies caps while at the club, where he spent three seasons before moving to the Melbourne Rebels, but his career is set to come full circle.

Rugby.title: Peebles Rugby Sevens Festival partners with community groups
Rugby.summary: Peebles Rugby Sevens Festival partners with community groups Peeblesshire News
Rugby.body:
PEEBLES Rugby Sevens Festival returns from Friday (July 31) to Sunday, August 2, bringing a fantastic weekend of rugby, entertainment and community spirit to the Gytes. This year, Peebles Rugby Football Club is delighted to support three local groups who will be taking part in the festival while raising funds for their own exciting initiatives.

Newlands Centre, a fantastic local community hub offering services, activities and events, will be hosting a bouncy castle for younger festival-goers. The Peebles High School Tanzania Expedition 2027 group will also be fundraising as 32 students prepare to visit Moshi, Tanzania, where they will work alongside local communities by helping to build houses, supporting schools and planting trees to help combat climate change.

Rugby.title: Nine players whose stock rose massively this July in Nations Championship
Rugby.summary: Trends, stocks, bonds, and rising values. Terms more commonly linked to economics, yet appropriate in this context, as many players saw their value increase during the first month of the Nations Championship.
Rugby.body:
Trends, stocks, bonds, and rising values. Terms more commonly linked to economics, yet appropriate in this context, as many players saw their value increase during the first month of the Nations Championship.

From young and talented wonderkids like Fabien Brau-Boirie to already well-established Test Match operators, here are a few players who saw their stocks go up after July. If there were any remaining doubts, they were erased over this three-game stretch, with Immanuel Feyi-Waboso firmly establishing himself as deserving of a spot on England’s wing. Feyi-Waboso is pure electricity, channelling his refined footwork to slip through any defence, delivering results for England week-in, week-out, as seen by his Player of the Match performance against Argentina. But if you still hold some doubts, then have a look at his Nations Championship stats: six line breaks, 30 carries, 246 running metres, 27 defenders beaten, 16 successful aerial takedowns, one assist and two tries scored. One of the safest stocks to get in the Test Match player market.

Rugby.title: Katelyn Vaha'akolo scores 82nd-minute winner to secure Blues three-peat
Rugby.summary: The 2026 Super Rugby Aupiki decider had a familiar flavour to it, with two regions that love to do battle squaring off, as they had done so in the final the year before.
Rugby.body:
The 2026 Super Rugby Aupiki decider had a familiar flavour to it, with two regions that love to do battle squaring off, as they had done so in the final the year before. This time, Matatu hosted the Blues under the roof at One New Zealand Stadium, with the visitors out to claim a historic three-peat and the hosts hoping to kick off a new era with another famous title.

Rugby.title: Eight possible bolters for the All Blacks' 44-man squad to tour South Africa
Rugby.summary: The others, though, are up for debate, with the coaching staff weighing up whether to go for a 6-4 split of forwards to backs, or 7-3, as discussed last week in Auckland.
Rugby.body:
On Monday, July 27, All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie will name his 44-man squad to travel on the Greatest Rivalry Tour of South Africa. Next month’s tour, which includes four games against South African domestic sides and four Tests, the last of which is in Baltimore, will be a proper litmus test of where Rennie’s side are, less than a year out from the Rugby World Cup in Australia.

The All Blacks got through the three Nations Championship July fixtures without major injury, with Codie Taylor’s calf strain the only concern ahead of the tour. Assuming the 34-man squad are fit and available, Rennie will add ten players to the Nations Championship group to travel to South Africa.

Rugby.title: 'South Africa can widen the All Blacks' previously unseen faultlines'
Rugby.summary: While Dave Rennie made a positive start to his tenure as New Zealand head coach, a Test series in South Africa will expose any weakness.
Rugby.body:
It’s a little dramatic and cliched but there is no other way to frame what lies ahead as the All Blacks’ moment of truth. Having won three successive July Tests under new coach Dave Rennie, the All Blacks now face an eight-game tour of South Africa featuring four matches against the Stormers, Sharks, Bulls and Lions, and four Tests against the Springboks – three in the Republic and one in Baltimore, USA.

The tour is being marketed under the tagline The Greatest Rivalry and is the focal point of the 2026 season. It’s a nostalgic throwback and a test-the-waters play to see if there is fan appetite for an old-fashioned tour of this nature.

Rugby.summary: Gloucester chief executive officer Alex Brown says there are talks ongoing regarding new investment in the Prem club.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester chief executive officer Alex Brown says there are "talks ongoing" about new investment in the Prem club. The Cherry and Whites' most recent set of accounts, for the year to June 2025, showed an increase in losses from £516,355 to £2.91m.

"There is interest in Gloucester Rugby but our shareholders and board are very sensitive to who that investment might be," Brown told BBC Radio Gloucestershire. "It has to be right for the club, for the future and we'll take every opportunity that comes but there are talks going on about further investment."

Rugby.title: ACLs, clutches and non-contact: How Grace Deane is preparing for her second Leicester season
Rugby.summary: If there is a moment in her life that Grace Deane hasn’t filled with something worthwhile, then it is likely to be a surprise to those who know her best.
Rugby.body:
If there is a moment in her life that Grace Deane hasn’t filled with something worthwhile, then it is likely to be a surprise to those who know her best. The Leicester Tigers wing is about to embark on her second season at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, and there is plenty on her plate to juggle before the season starts in September.

The 26-year-olds priority is to complete her return to full fitness after she suffered an Anterior Cruciate Ligament [ACL] injury after only three matches for Tigers in 2025/26. She has been able to join in with most of the training sessions since preseason started but crucially isn’t allowed to take part in the contact sessions for now.

Rugby.title: Layla Sae: 'I am going to make the most of it when I do get back'
Rugby.summary: Just 16 minutes into Layla Sae's Harlequins and Premiership Women's Rugby debut last November she was tackled and heard a pop in her knee.
Rugby.body:
Just 16 minutes into Layla Sae’s Harlequins and Premiership Women’s Rugby debut last November she was tackled and heard a pop in her knee. The New Zealand international got back to her feet and tried to continue but she was taken off and later told she had a grade three ACL tear.

Sae’s first reaction to the news was shock and she was “gutted”. Because just a week after relocating to London, alongside international teammate Liana Mikaele-Tu’u, her PWR journey was over.

Rugby.body:
The Monaco Rugby Federation’s U18 team was crowned European runners-up last weekend in Budapest, securing promotion to the Championship, the highest division of European rugby sevens. This historic achievement puts Monaco among the 12 best nations in European U18 rugby sevens.

Only one year after winning the Trophy 2 title to earn promotion to Trophy 1, the young team claimed a silver medal in Hungary. Following a strong tournament, the team was beaten only by Latvia in the final. Despite not claiming the title, Monaco still secured promotion to the Championship alongside Latvia.

Rugby.summary: Gloucester finished eighth in the PREM last season, having not been higher up the table at any point during the campaign, and were 31 points off the play-off places.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester Rugby CEO Alex Brown says talks are ‘ongoing’ to bring desperately needed fresh investment into the club, after a loss of £2.91 million was reported for the 2024/25 financial year.

While Brown says some of the losses – up from £516,000 the year before – can be attributed to ‘accounting nuances’ around the way academy license payments are made, there are fears that unless they can find a new backer, the Cherry and Whites will be left behind their English rivals.

Rugby.title: Ex-All Black captain Todd Blackadder replaced as head coach of Toshiba
Rugby.summary: Former All Blacks captain Todd Blackadder's long reign as head coach of Toshiba Brave Lupus is over, with the 54-year-old being moved 'upstairs' by the Fuchu-based team.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks captain Todd Blackadder’s long reign as head coach of Toshiba Brave Lupus is over, with the 54-year-old being moved ‘upstairs’ by the Fuchu-based team. Having been appointed in April 2019, Blackadder was one of the longest-serving head coaches in Japan’s Rugby League One, but Brave Lupus have opted to change their coaching team following a disappointing season.

Blackadder led Brave Lupus to back-to-back titles in 2024 and 2025 but they fell short of completing a three-peat in 2026, exiting the competition at the quarter-final stage after an injury-disrupted campaign.

Rugby.title: Antonio Prim on taking Portugal to new heights with historic Nations Cup wins
Rugby.summary: Prop Antonio Prim, 23, says Os Lobos seek to be groundbreakers, elevating Portuguese rugby to places it's never been before.
Rugby.body:
Rapidly improving Portugal has a clear brief about its goals in international rugby. Prop Antonio Prim, 23, says Os Lobos seek to be groundbreakers, elevating Portuguese rugby to places it’s never been before.

Giddy heights were reached at the 2023 Rugby World Cup when Portugal stunned Fiji 24-23. But by 2025, progress had stalled after a record 106-7 loss to Ireland. Earlier this month, Portugal ended their recent World Rugby Nations Cup campaign with an upset 32-28 victory over Tonga in Winnipeg. It was their first win over Tonga and came a week after beating Canada 38-14, following a narrow 30-29 loss to the USA.

Rugby.title: Blues re-sign 'well-respected leader' Taufa Funaki
Rugby.summary: The Blues have locked down halfback Taufa Funaki on a new two-year deal in their latest off-season move.
Rugby.body:
The Blues have locked down halfback Taufa Funaki on a new two-year deal in their latest off-season move. Funaki has played 42 games for his hometown team, with seven tries. A Sacred Heart College product, the 25-year-old former New Zealand U20 player’s signature comes as the club loses stalwart Sam Nock after 11 seasons representing the City of Sails.

Funaki was a big contributor to the drought-breaking 2024 Super Rugby Pacific title run, and says he is excited to return for another two seasons. “I grew up in Auckland dreaming of wearing the Blues jersey, so to be able to continue that journey and keep representing the 09 is something I’m grateful for,” he said.

However, one Kiwi pundit believes there are only two starting jerseys yet to be claimed.

With three Tests now under Dave Rennie’s belt as All Blacks head coach, he and his selectors have fielded 33 players, with just Kyle Preston, Simon Parker and Beauden Barrett the squad members left out during the July slate.

Holland dislocated his shoulder just minutes into his first preseason run for the Highlanders, and has spent the last five months rehabbing the injury.

Rugby.title: Saracens appoint Coetzee as new chief executive
Rugby.summary: Premiership side Saracens appoint South African Ed Coetzee as their new chief executive officer following similar roles at Brive and Sharks.
Rugby.body:
Prem Rugby side Saracens have appointed former Sharks and Bayonne prop Ed Coetzee as the club's new chief executive officer. The 46-year-old made more than 300 appearances in professional rugby, playing four seasons for the Sharks in South Africa, before six years in France at Bayonne and Biarritz.

He then moved into administration, becoming commercial and marketing director at Sharks before taking over as chief operating officer (COO) and then CEO in 2019. Coetzee has been CEO at Brive since 2024, and replaces Charlie Beall who stepped down at the StoneX stadium at the end of the 2025-26 season.

Rugby.title: Springboks fans have never been humble
Rugby.summary: Springboks fans have never been humble... A few years ago, Henry Pollock told me that he wanted to be “spoken about as a great of the game”.
Rugby.body:
A few years ago, Henry Pollock told me that he wanted to be “spoken about as a great of the game”. He explained that one goal was simply an opportunity to move the posts further back. Winning a junior World Cup, making his international debut, beating New Zealand, lifting the Webb Ellis Cup and being named World Player of the Year were all merely “stepping stones”.

Imagine the response if Pollock had actually said any of that. Picture the frothing replies, the bulging veins, the sudden concern for endangered values of rugby. Who does this blond English child think he is? Someone should wipe that smirk off his face.

Rugby.title: RFU introduce toolkit to combat sexism and misogyny at community clubs
Rugby.summary: The Rugby Football Union have partnered with Women in Sport to launch a landmark anti-sexism and misogyny policy to make the sport more inclusive for women's and girls.
Rugby.body:
The Rugby Football Union have partnered with Women in Sport to launch a landmark anti-sexism and misogyny policy to make the sport more inclusive for women’s and girls. Research conducted by the two parties, which included the feedback of over 600 volunteers associated with community clubs in England, have highlighted the scale of sexism and misogyny in the sport at grassroots level.

Quantitative and qualitative evidence gathered from volunteers across the 2025/26 season found that 83 per cent of female respondents had experienced sexism, while a quarter of female match officials reported that they had frequently experienced or witnessed sexist behaviour.

Rugby.title: 'My words had impact': How Laura Delgado is finding her feet in full-time coaching
Rugby.summary: Tuesday 30 June 2026. A day that I will never forget. The day that I became a full-time coach.
Rugby.body:
Tuesday 30 June 2026. A day that I will never forget. The day that I became a full-time coach. 48 hours before arriving in the USA, I was playing for the Barbarians in my last official game at Allianz Stadium. I shared the locker room with so many friends and colleagues. After the game, I went to the Harlequins cottages to get my things and boarded the plane, my destination set for Minneapolis, to join Women’s Elite Rugby’s Twin Cities Gemini as an assistant.

It was an intense start to this new adventure. I headed straight to practice after arriving. The girls were incredible from the get-go. However, I have to say it was weird to be involved in a training session without being a player. After so many years working on my skills, honing my scrummaging abilities, I was there to solely coach and help players become better.

Rugby.title: Recently retired Wales legend Leigh Halfpenny confirms club future
Rugby.summary: Leigh Halfpenny, who hung up his boots at the end of last season, will remain at Cardiff Arms Park next season after being appointed first-team kicking coach and skills coach within the academy set-up.
Rugby.body:
Leigh Halfpenny, who hung up his boots at the end of last season, will remain at Cardiff Arms Park next season after being appointed first-team kicking coach and skills coach within the academy set-up.

Halfpenny, 37, recently helped Wales as a kicking coach for the first three rounds of the Nations Championship and scored 570 points in 90 appearances for the Blue & Blacks. He won 101 caps for Wales, three Six Nations titles, including two Grand Slams, and sits third on the all-time men’s points list with 801 and admits that the club means a huge amount to him.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper should consider himself very fortunate as he's given wildcard into Canadian Open
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper should consider himself very fortunate as he's given wildcard into Canadian Open Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper is a supremely talented individual, and someone more than capable of challenging for Grand Slam titles eventually. This is a fact that felt almost certain just over a year ago, but now feels like a distant memory.

After surging into the US Open semi-finals, and following that up with a maiden Masters 1000 title at Indian Wells, the Brit had stamped himself on the map with emphasis. People were justifiably backing him as the next in line to break up Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner’s duopoly with his big-serving left-handed game that had already scored big wins over the former.

Tennis.body:
Former British No1 Jack Draper has been named as a wild card for an upcoming tournament as he continues to recover from an arm injury. The 24-year-old has missed all three grand slam tournaments so far this year through injury, but will hope to feature at the National Bank Open.

Draper was scheduled to feature at Wimbledon, where he would have faced Taylor Fritz in the first round, only to withdraw from the grand slam at SW19 around 24 hours before the match was due to begin. The former world No4 withdrew from the tournament due to an arm injury, which forced him to miss the French Open and the Australian Open earlier in the year. The National Bank Open is set to get underway in Canada next week, and Draper has been confirmed as a wild card entrant for the tournament.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper Withdraws from Washington, Gets Montreal Wildcard: Return as Early as Monday?
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper Withdraws from Washington, Gets Montreal Wildcard: Return as Early as Monday? TennisTemple
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper could be back on the courts much sooner than expected. Forced to withdraw from Washington after a recurrence of his left arm injury, the Briton has nonetheless received a wildcard for the Masters 1000 in Montreal, which begins next Monday.

This announcement comes as a surprise. Present in Washington in recent days, Draper had even practiced before pulling out of the tournament due to renewed arm pain. However, this withdrawal appears to have been more a precautionary measure than a sign of his injury worsening. His wildcard for Montreal suggests he could be ready to compete again as early as next week.

Tennis.title: Ekaterina Alexandrova collapses on court during three-hour match against Kristina Liutova at WTA Memphis Tennis Classic
Tennis.summary: Ekaterina Alexandrova collapses on court during three-hour match against Kristina Liutova at WTA Memphis Tennis Classic Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Ekaterina Alexandrova collapsed on court in the third set of her WTA Tour match against Kristina Liutova at the Memphis Tennis Classic. Alexandrova, who was top seed at the tournament, was 5-4 down in the third set of a three-hour match in temperatures that reached 34 degrees Celsius, when the match had to be stopped and she had a lengthy treatment.

Tennis.body:
Cruz Hewitt - the 17-year-old son of former world number one Lleyton Hewitt - earned his first ATP victory in his main singles draw debut. The Australian beat fellow qualifier Marcos Giron of the United States 6-3 6-4 in 74 minutes.

His maiden win came at the Washington Open - a competition his father won in 2004. It was one of his father's 30 career titles, including the 2002 Wimbledon men's singles crown.

Tennis.title: Alexandrova collapses on court amid 34C heat
Tennis.summary: World number 19 Ekaterina Alexandrova collapses on court and had to retire from her first-round match at the Memphis Classic due to high temperatures.
Tennis.body:
World number 19 Ekaterina Alexandrova collapsed on court and had to retire from her first-round match at the Memphis Classic due to high temperatures. Russian Alexandrova, who was the number one seed, was trailing 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 5-4 against 16-year-old compatriot Kristina Liutova in a match where temperatures reached 34C.

The match was initially paused as Alexandrova tried to continue, before she received a time violation as she took too long to serve amid her struggles. But in the middle of the next point, Alexandrova fell to the ground and needed immediate medical attention.

By his own admission, the arm injury which has derailed Jack Draper's career is "complicated". Former British number one Draper withdrew from a planned comeback in Washington on Monday after feeling more discomfort from bone bruising in his serving arm.

It is a similar situation to what happened at Wimbledon last month, where the 24-year-old Englishman also spoke positively about his fitness - and seemingly practised well - before pulling out on the eve of the tournament.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper withdraws on eve of match again as injury worries mount
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper withdraws on eve of match again as injury worries mount Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper's injury concerns have deepened after he withdrew on the eve of a match for the second time in a row. Draper pulled out of an ATP Tour event in Washington on Monday, the day before his first-round match. It followed the 24-year-old ruling himself out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament, despite saying he felt positive about his fitness.

The former British No 1 has a long-term arm injury and has played just 14 matches in the past 12 months. He continues to be hampered by a bruised humerus. Draper is in a race against time to prove his fitness, with the US Open mixed doubles event taking place on August 25 and 26, where he is paired with Jessica Pegula. The singles draw starts on August 30. He is targeting tournaments in Montreal and Cincinnati as part of his preparations.

Tennis.title: Norrie wins first match since April
Tennis.summary: British number two Cameron Norrie ends a six-match losing streak with a straight-set win over Aleksandar Kovacevic.
Tennis.body:
British number two Cameron Norrie ended a six-match losing streak with a 6-4-6-1 win over Aleksandar Kovacevic in the first round of the Mifel Open in Mexico. Norrie had not won since the Madrid Open in April, a run which included a first-round exit to qualifier Michael Zheng at Wimbledon.

Playing at the tournament in Los Cobos where he won his first ATP title in 2021, Norrie recovered from having his serve broken twice in the first set, including in the opening game.

Tennis.title: Injured Draper withdraws on eve of another tournament
Tennis.summary: Former British number one Jack Draper withdraws from another event because of issues around his recurring long-term arm injury.
Tennis.body:
Former British number one Jack Draper has withdrawn on the eve of another tournament because of the long-term arm injury which continues to cause him discomfort. Left-handed Draper, 24, has pulled out of the ATP Tour event in Washington, which was set to be his first appearance since ruling himself out of Wimbledon last month.

Draper has been hampered by bone bruising in his serving arm for more than a year, but said at the weekend, external he was "feeling physically good" before the Mubadala DC Open.

Tennis.title: Sabalenka & Djokovic to team up in US Open mixed doubles
Tennis.summary: Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka pair up for the US Open mixed doubles, which was controversially revamped last year to include superstar pairings.
Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka are set to play together in the upcoming US Open mixed doubles, which was controversially revamped last year to include superstar pairings. Serbia's Djokovic, 39, and 28-year-old Belarusian Sabalenka are set to join forces for the two-day event, which starts on 25 August in New York.

Former British number one Jack Draper is planning to reunite with American Jessica Pegula after they made the 2025 semi-finals, while Poland's Iga Swiatek and Norway's Casper Ruud - last year's runners-up - will also team up again.

Tennis.body:
Jack Draper has withdrawn from the DC Open with a left arm injury. The former world No 4 has endured a injury-strewn 2026 which saw him miss both the French Open and Wimbledon, with the withdrawal coming just days after Draper claiming that he feels "really physically good".

The Brit, who is coached by Sir Andy Murray, has dropped to world No 147 on the ATP Tour rankings and that will likely mean he will need to qualify if he is to play at this September's US Open, having missed out on the main draw for the event.

Tennis.title: US Open 2026 mixed doubles: Are Carlos Alcaraz and Emma Raducanu playing in star-studded event?
Tennis.summary: US Open 2026 mixed doubles: Are Carlos Alcaraz and Emma Raducanu playing in star-studded event? London Evening Standard
Tennis.body:
Last year saw some of the biggest names in both the men’s and women’s games join forces for a newly-shaped event aimed at bringing more eyes to doubles as a discipline. The US Tennis Association (USTA) confirmed that Arthur Ashe Stadium was sold out across the draw’s two days during ‘Fan Week’ at Flushing Meadows, which is held in the days leading up to the main singles competitions.

Novak Djokovic was joined by compatriot Olga Danilovic while world No1 Jannik Sinner was set to play with doubles specialist Katerina Siniakova before the Italian withdrew, having retired from his Cincinnati final against Alcaraz with illness the day previously.

Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka will pair up in the mixed doubles at the US Open. Women's world No 1 Sabalenka and 24-time Grand Slam champion Djokovic will join forces in the mixed doubles event, which was won by Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori in both 2024 and 2025.

Tennis.title: Greg Rusedski suggests if he believes Jack Draper deserves a US Open wildcard this year
Tennis.summary: Greg Rusedski suggests if he believes Jack Draper deserves a US Open wildcard this year Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper has had a torrid time of late, desperately unfortunate with his fitness routinely failing. It seems like every time he seemed to be reaching the light at the end of the tunnel, a new setback would occur from seemingly nowhere, resulting in a chain of events that has sent him falling down the world rankings with some speed.

His current position is not indicative of the player he is, and the hope is that he can prove that in the coming months. That being said, Draper’s decision to register for a Challenger event whilst the Canadian and Cincinnati Open are on is a bold one that will not help him rise any quicker. Minutes on the court are clearly his priority.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu suffers significant ranking drop ahead of the US swing starting
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu suffers significant ranking drop ahead of the US swing starting Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu has faced another setback ahead of the North American hard court swing getting underway. Raducanu reached the Queen’s final last month, which enabled her to climb back up to world number 31 and she was in a seeded position for Wimbledon.

However, the Briton was unable to even take to the court for her home major, as Raducanu withdrew from Wimbledon due to a stress fracture in her right leg. Raducanu is still unable to compete and her ranking has now suffered as a result of her absence.

Tennis.title: Britain's Jones defends Challenger title in Palermo
Tennis.summary: Britain's Francesca Jones makes it back-to-back wins on the Challenger Tour by successfully defending her title at the Palermo Ladies Open.
Tennis.body:
Britain's Francesca Jones made it back-to-back wins on the Challenger Tour by successfully defending her title at the Palermo Ladies Open. The top seed beat Fiona Ferro 6-0 4-6 7-6 (8-6) in two hours and 43 minutes.

Jones, who had dropped one set all tournament, took the opener in just 21 minutes. The 25-year-old then fought back from 3-0 down to lead 4-3 in the second, but Ferro reeled off three straight games to level the match.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper entrusts himself to Andy Murray to become himself again: "He believes a lot in me"
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper entrusts himself to Andy Murray to become himself again: "He believes a lot in me" Punto de Break
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper faces alongside Andy Murray a decisive stage to relaunch his career after injuries have slowed down his progress. The British player will make his return at the ATP 500 in Washington thanks to a wildcard, currently ranked 147th in the world, and acknowledges that working with one of his big idols is giving him confidence and new perspectives.

There are few players whose current ranking reflects their true potential worse than Jack Draper. The Brit has shown that, when his body allows him to compete consistently, he has the weapons to establish himself among the elite. However, recurrent physical issues have turned that consistency into his major challenge and have pushed him far from the positions that would correspond to his tennis level.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper Looks Ahead To Latest Comeback In Washington
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper Looks Ahead To Latest Comeback In Washington ubitennis.net
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper says he is feeling physically better than at any other stage during the past 12 months ahead of his return to action at an ATP 500 event in Washington. The former world No.4 has been troubled by injury setbacks in recent times, which have resulted in him only being able to play five tournaments so far this year. Draper suffered bone bruising in his serving arm last summer and ended up missing a chunk of the Tour between 2025 and 2026. Then during this year’s European clay swing, he picked up a knee injury that sidelined him for a few more weeks.

Draper, who has won one Masters 1000 title so far in his career, looked to be getting back in shape towards the end of June after reaching the semi-finals in Eastbourne. He then travelled to Wimbledon to conduct his usual pre-tournament media commitments before withdrawing from his home Grand Slam due to a flare-up of his arm issue.
